clean.tx: arɨkʷajõ asisi aapi ata sekoa kõtkõra tekeri
clean.tl: Arɨkʷajõ got corn seed from Kõtkõrã's house.

clean.tx: sete isoa ajẽeri te kẽrã asisi ko
clean.tl: (Then) he looked, (and thought): “Where does he (the bird) eat corn?”
Then (he said to this daughters): “I will follow him, my daughters.”

clean.tx: soa kot kaap te pekaat soa kot
clean.tl: “I will look to see, I will look at that.”

clean.tx: atɨ sete sitõpna tõpna sekoa pɨbot kõtkõra taap
clean.tl: Poor guy, he followed him all the way until he arrived at Kõtkõrã's (Cicada's) village.’ (Arɨkʷajõ followed the bird all the way to Kõtkõra's house)
He (Arɨkʷajõ) entered the house, sat himself down, and was given food.
He sat down, then got up, and stayed around there.

clean.tx: ma te kẽra eke aose sesetara ke te Kõtkõra takiat
clean.tl: “When is that man leaving?” said Kõtkõrã's daughters.

clean.tx: te ka aose asisi 'ata naat kop
clean.tl: Through his mind, the man is carrying off the corn.’ (Lit. ‘It comes from him, the man is taking the corn.’)

clean.tx: tapsɨtbõ i'ata asisibõ i'ata arakʷibõ i'ata komatabõ i'ata kaat naat kop aose
clean.tl: He got manioc, corn, peanuts, beans, he stayed there doing that (taking everything), the man (i.e., Arɨkʷajõ).
Then, when he had already got it all, he left again.
“Where is your mother?”

clean.tx: osesi jãõbõ ka te ikão taaga kit ata naat te kiikona taaga kit ata
clean.tl: “Our mother went over there at that time to get walking palm's seed for us to eat, get walking palm's seed,” (they replied).

clean.tx: poret ejatota ipekara taaga kit atatkʷa nop pegat
clean.tl: “Then, go call her, it is no longer necessary to bring walking palm seed” (Arɨkʷajõ told his daughters).

clean.tx: kiopap ta eba jẽ eba kaateri imaa ke te kiɨape kieba motkʷa ke te sɨraapna
clean.tl: “Our corn is here, make our beverage from it, and prepare the manioc to make (our) massaco.”
They heard him, the daughters, then they left, went straight there and arrived (where their mother was).

clean.tx: akʷa kɨp perek piora naat kop
clean.tl: She was digging for wild cará tubers.
“Our father called you, mother.”

clean.tx: kiɨape ma ke te kiopaperi ita kaat ikão
clean.tl: “(Call her) to make our chicha from our corn here, that (is what he) said at that time.”
“To prepare manioc to make massaco,” that (is what he) said at that time.

clean.tx: erek tɨɨna sitoabip etoabip tõet ejattaɨpiat sara aose igoterõp sete
clean.tl: She said: “Poor bastard, I doubt he has a crop. You poor children, he is a man who has nothing.”’ (Lit. ‘She said: “Pitied one, I doubt his crop (exists). Poor people of your children, this man has nothing.”’)
They went again, his daughters.
“Mom said just that.” (And, thus, the daughters told their father what their mother had said.)

clean.tx: ke ebõ te setaɨpkʷa paat te
clean.tl: “It is like that now (she is angry at me), but she'll calm down."
“She is still going to laugh,” he (said).’ (That is what Arɨkʷajõ thought about his wife.)

clean.tx: pia setoa arẽp te aramira 'ipat neara
clean.tl: He stayed there waiting, then the woman came back again.
She was angry, poor Pãrarekosa.

clean.tx: poget kop peropka peakʷa kɨp perek
clean.tl: She stayed there, and then went to cook wild cará tubers.
She ate, and stayed there the way she was (angry), until it got dark.
Then it dawned.
(After that Arɨkʷajõ came and said to his children:) ‘“I will cure your beverage.”
“You can drink! Drink!”
“I am going to make your teeth fall out.”
It happened really that way, their teeth fell out.
“It won't be hard, your food, my daughters.”’ (This sentence continues the speech of Arɨkʷajõ to his children.)

clean.tx: kaatna'ẽp poret koap koapna te kijãj pogeti poret
clean.tl: They stayed that way, our teeth, in order for us to eat.’ (Lit. ‘They became that way in order to be (our) eating instrument, our teeth stayed that way.')

clean.tx: kaatna te te kijãj ipẽtna ke nop
clean.tl: That's why our teeth are not hard,’ (Lit. ‘In being that way really, our teeth are not hard.')
They just drop out (and grow again).
It is always just that way.’ (‘The cycle keeps repeating itself, it is always like that.’)
That's how our teeth are.

clean.tx: kaapese naat aapi õsop te asisi
clean.tl: That is how (they) found corn seed.
And that's how it appeared the things that we eat.
(But) that's how it was at those times.

clean.tx: kõtkõraropna aropõ te asisi naat eteet
clean.tl: If it were not for Kõtkõra, there would be nothing, no corn. (All edible things were first planted by Kõtkõra, who was also a shaman).
(There would be) no corn.

clean.tx: aropõ te piro tapsɨt akʷa kʷaako piroap
clean.tl: There wouldn't be anything, no yucca, no cará tuber, no sweet potato.
If it were up to Arɨkʷajõ, he wouldn't own anything.
He possessed nothing.
If it were not for this man (Kõtkõrã), (there would be nothing.)
It's finished.

flagged.tl: The black-fronted piping guan bird (that was around) defecated inside the house.

flagged.tx: pia setoa õẽp te kʷako seset neara
flagged.tl: He (Arɨkʷajõ) stayed there waiting for the black-fronted piping guan bird to come back.
